# Design to build workflow

How a visual design becomes React code in this repository. Four artifacts are involved and only one of them is the source of truth, so the first job of this document is to say which one and why. Written 2026-08-12 during the build phase 4.8 design review, and applicable to any future phase whose deliverable is visual rather than behavioural.

For the twelve-stage cadence itself, read `../Build_workflow_cadence.md` one level up. This document sits on top of it and answers a narrower question: what does a builder actually build against when the deliverable is a look.

## Start here: the prototype

`design-system/prototype/app.html` is a working, clickable prototype of the whole product in a single file. It is the centre of this workflow, and the thing to open first.

It runs the real journey: the disclaimer gate, the landing screen, a typed or seeded question, the animated pipeline advancing through Guard, Think, Plan, Act and Write with tool chips landing as each tool fires, the answer typing in with its provenance spine growing alongside, expandable source cards, the feedback surface, the guest allowance counting down, the soft login prompt, and the sign-in wall. Four questions are canned end to end, with different layer mixes so the colour system is visible in use.

It exists in three places, all from the same source file:

| Where | For |
|-------|-----|
| The Claude Design project "NCBI Agentic Search", under Prototype | Playing with it, and changing it |
| `design-system/prototype/app.html` in the repository | The version under git, pulled from Claude Design |
| A published artifact URL | Sending to people. Generated by `make_prototype_artifact.py`, never hand-edited |

That third one is generated rather than copied on purpose. The artifact host supplies its own document skeleton, so the page needs a slightly different shape to publish, and doing that transform by hand would create exactly the silent drift this document exists to prevent. Run `python3 docs/build/design/make_prototype_artifact.py` after every pull and the two can never disagree.

## The four pieces

| Artifact | What it is | Who reads it |
|----------|-----------|--------------|
| `design-system/prototype/app.html` | The prototype. The whole product, clickable, in one file | The product owner plays with it. People are shown it. No builder reads it as a spec |
| `design-system/` (the cards) | The blueprints. 18 isolated cards: brand, foundations, identity, components, screens, flows | Builders build from it. Judges verify against it |
| `Phase_4.8_visual_design.html` | The argument. One scroll explaining why the system looks the way it does | Anyone who needs the reasoning rather than the result |
| Bossman mode | The build crew and the inspectors | Runs the twelve-stage cadence and produces the React code |

The distinction that matters: the prototype and the pitch page are both allowed to go stale, because neither is what the code is checked against. The component cards are not allowed to go stale, because the premise gate asserts against them.

That split is worth stating plainly, because it is the one thing people get wrong. The prototype shows how the product behaves. The cards define what each piece must look like. A builder implementing the citation chip reads `identity/citation-chip.html`, not the prototype, because the card is the isolated, unambiguous statement of that one component. The prototype is where you find out whether the whole thing feels right.

The design system's structure, as of 2026-08-12:

| Group | Cards |
|-------|-------|
| Prototype | The whole product, clickable. Not a component card |
| Brand | Logo |
| Foundations | Colour, Type, Spacing and shape |
| Identity | Layer badges, Citation chip, Provenance spine |
| Components | App bar, Search bar, Pipeline stepper, Source card, Trust signals, Feedback |
| Screens | Home, Streaming, Answer |
| Flows | Guest flow, Disclaimer modal |

## How the design system plugs into bossman

This is the part worth understanding, because it is what stops a builder from styling things however it feels like.

Every build phase here has a blocking premise gate at stage 5: write the test, watch it fail, then build. For a visual phase the obvious problem is that you cannot unit-test "looks good." The resolution is that the design system files become the thing the gate asserts against.

Four assertions, in descending order of how load-bearing they are:

- Token conformance: the MUI theme's palette must exactly equal the hex values in `foundations/colors.html`. If a builder nudges a blue, the gate fails. This is the cheapest check and it catches the most common drift.
- Structure: a citation chip must carry a layer class. A source card must render all six provenance fields. Testable, and it catches a builder quietly dropping the license field because it was fiddly.
- Contrast: WCAG 2.1 AA on every token pair actually used. The repository already has `@axe-core/playwright`, so this is real and automated rather than a promise to check later.
- Assembly: every screen is reachable in the running app, a signed-in question reaches the API, and the screens render from the resulting event stream rather than from a timer. This replaced a planned visual-regression check: no screenshot test was built, and leaving the promise in place advertised a gate nothing performed. Pixel fidelity is deliberately not gated and is the judge and adversary rounds' job, which `tracker/phase_4.8.md` states in its own coverage section.

So the answer to "how do the two connect" is that the design system is not documentation, it is a fixture. Bossman reads it as input and the gates read it as the expected output.

This is the same discipline `goal-contracts` already requires elsewhere: the verify surface has to exist and be immutable before the loop starts. A visual phase without a fixture library has no verify surface at all, which is exactly how a restyle turns into an argument about taste at review time.

## The loop when a design changes

The round trip, in order:

1. The product owner edits a card in the Claude Design project "NCBI Agentic Search". This is the only place design changes originate.
2. The change is pulled with `DesignSync` and written into `docs/build/design/design-system/`, which is a true one-to-one mirror. Nothing is interpreted at this step.
3. `python3 docs/build/design/make_prototype_artifact.py` regenerates the publishable prototype page, and it is republished to its existing artifact URL. This is the link shared with people.
4. If the change also affects the argument, it is applied by hand to `Phase_4.8_visual_design.html`, which is a separate narrative document rather than a generated view of anything.

The four artifacts, and how each one stays current:

| Artifact | Where it lives | How it syncs |
|----------|---------------|--------------|
| Claude Design project | Cloud, `claude.ai/design` | Source of truth. The product owner edits here and nowhere else |
| `docs/build/design/design-system/` | Repo, under git | One-to-one mirror, pulled with `DesignSync`. Exact, no interpretation |
| `design-system/prototype/app.html` | Repo, under git | Part of the same one-to-one mirror. This is the clickable prototype |
| `Phase_4.8_prototype.html` | Repo, under git | Generated from the prototype card by `make_prototype_artifact.py`. Never hand-edited |
| `Phase_4.8_visual_design.html` | Repo, under git | Hand-maintained narrative. Shares the tokens, not the content. Allowed to lag |
| The published artifacts | Cloud, two stable URLs | One for the prototype, one for the argument. Republished from their HTML files |

One point that decides where a builder looks: builders and gates read `docs/build/design/design-system/`, the repository copy, never the Claude Design project directly. Bossman runs locally, the premise gate asserts against files on disk, and only the repository copy is under version control and reviewable in a pull request. The cloud project is where the design is authored; the repository mirror is what the build is held to.

The consequence is that a design change is not real until it has been pulled. A card edited in Claude Design and not yet mirrored is invisible to every builder and every gate, and the build will correctly produce the old design.

From there the cost depends entirely on timing:

- Before the phase opens: free. Change anything, costs nothing, no code exists yet.
- After the phase opens: expensive. A spec change means the premise gate changes and every affected ticket reopens.

That second row is the same reason this repository froze `PRD.md` and `Technical_specification.md` before build started. A specification that moves during a build is not a specification, it is a conversation, and the gates cannot hold against a conversation.

The practical rule: settle the design first, then open the phase. Treat the design system as frozen for the duration of the phase, the same way the tech spec is, and route anything that surfaces mid-build to a follow-up rather than editing the fixture underneath a running gate.

## The sequence

Stage zero, the design review. Not a build. No branch, no tickets, no bossman. The product owner reacts to the pitch page, pushes things around in Claude Design, and the two sides go back and forth until nothing more wants changing. This stage has no cadence and no gates on purpose.

Stage one onward, the build. The design freezes, `phase/4.8-web-ui-visual-design` opens, and the normal twelve-stage cadence in `Build_workflow_cadence.md` takes over with the design system as its fixture.

## What build phase 4.8 looks like

Roughly twelve tickets, in dependency order:

| Ticket | Delivers |
|--------|----------|
| 1 | MUI and Emotion added, supply-chain checked per `supply-chain-security` |
| 2 | The theme, generated from `foundations/` tokens |
| 3 | App shell: app bar, logo, disclaimer strip, footer |
| 4 | Home screen |
| 5 | Citation chip and source card |
| 6 | Pipeline stepper and tool chips |
| 7 | Trust pills and the refusal state |
| 8 | Provenance spine |
| 9 | Disclaimer modal |
| 10 | Guest-flow states, styled with the backend stubbed |
| 11 | Auth screens restyled |
| 12 | Accessibility pass |

One hard constraint belongs in the premise gate: the 120 existing frontend tests stay green. This phase is a restyle. If behaviour changes, something went wrong.

Two items are deliberately designed here and wired elsewhere, so neither one moves the locked build order:

| Item | Styled in | Wired in |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Guest flow: anonymous sessions, the search allowance, history migration on login | 4.8 | 4.5, 4.6 and 6.0, which already own those scopes |
| Feedback: answer rating, reason chips, the per-citation "does not support" flag | 4.8 | 4.6, which already names feedback as an `interactions` field |

## Adapting the build to the UI

The product owner authors the UI. This section exists because the first pull got the
polarity wrong and treated the design as claims to be trimmed until they fit the
backend. That is backwards. The design is the target, and a gap between it and the
backend is work to plan, not a caption to delete.

One category is exempt, by agreement: factual content. A tool name that does not
exist, a promise the system cannot keep, a statistic that is not real. Those are
corrected on the pull without ceremony, because they are wrong rather than ahead.
Everything else the design asks for is a requirement.

Every surface the prototype defines sorts into one of three tiers. The tier decides
what build phase 4.8 does with it, not whether it gets built.

### Tier A: 4.8 ships it complete

The backend already exists on `develop`. These are styling work and nothing else.

| Surface | Backed by |
|---------|-----------|
| Landing, question submission | The core loop, plus the REST and SSE adapter from build phase 4.0 |
| Run screen: pipeline stepper, tool chips, stop | The typed event contract already emits a step event per node and a `tool_start` per call; cancellation shipped in 4.0 |
| Answer: streamed text, citation chips, source cards with provenance fields | Build phases 2.2 and 3.4 |
| Trust pills, risk tier, conflict disclosure | Build phase 3.4 |
| Refusal, and the out-of-scope refusal | Build phase 3.0's guardrail |
| Show work, the per-run trace | The same events the stepper reads |
| Sign in, sign out, the account menu | Build phase 1.1 |
| About page, rail, toasts, copy to clipboard | Frontend only |

### Tier B: 4.8 ships the UI, an already-planned phase wires it

The design is built in full and reads from a local stub. The owning phase later
swaps the stub for a real call, and the UI does not change when it does.

| Surface | Wired by |
|---------|----------|
| Follow-up questions and their suggested hints | 4.5, bounded session memory (Decision F) |
| Conversation history, archiving a run | 4.5 for the session, 4.6 for persistence into `interactions` |
| Feedback: rating, reason chips, the per-citation flag | 4.6, which already names feedback as an `interactions` field |
| KGX export request | 4.4, specified as a batch job rather than a live adapter |
| Guest allowance, the counter, the sign-in wall | 6.0 for the limit itself. The data model already supports the flow: `interactions.user_id` is nullable so a session can start anonymous and attach to an account at signup |

Stubbing rule: a stub returns plausible local data and is visibly marked in code, never
in the interface. A user or a demo audience must not be able to tell a stubbed surface
from a live one, because the point of 4.8 is that the product looks finished.

### Tier C: 4.8 ships the UI, nothing owns the backend yet

These are real capability gaps the design surfaced. Each needs a home before it can be
wired, and naming that home is a product-owner decision rather than something to assume.

| Surface | What is missing |
|---------|-----------------|
| API key issuance, reveal, copy, rotate | `auth/` implements bearer JWT for a browser session. An issued, long-lived, revocable key for the REST, MCP, command-line and export surfaces does not exist and is not in Section 25's build order |
| Developer docs, seven sub-pages | Not specified as a surface anywhere. The content is largely static prose, so 4.8 can ship it, but it needs a named owner for accuracy, since a docs page that drifts from the API is worse than no docs page |

### What this means for the phase

Build phase 4.8 builds every screen in the prototype, all seven, plus the docs
sub-pages. Nothing is deferred on the grounds that its backend is not ready. The
ticket list grows from the original twelve to cover the surfaces the design added:
follow-ups, history, the account menu, the API key panel, the docs screen and the rail.

The premise gate gains one clause because of this section: a stubbed surface must be
indistinguishable from a live one in the rendered output, and every stub must be
registered in one place so the phase that wires it can find it without a search.

## Settled decisions

Three design choices gated this phase, since each one changes at least one ticket above. All three were settled by the product owner on 2026-08-12 and are recorded in `DECISIONS.md`.

| Decision | Outcome | Ticket |
|----------|---------|--------|
| Provenance spine | Keep, always rendered. A segmented vertical track beside the answer, one segment per claim, coloured by the layer that backed it. Kept always-on rather than only-on-problem, because a track that appears solely when something is wrong is a track nobody has learned to read | 8 |
| Navy hero | Keep. The single saturated surface in the system, with everything else restrained so this one can be loud | 4 |
| Monospace identifiers | Keep, narrowed. Monospace marks a string transcribed exactly. Gene symbols are excluded | 2, and every ticket rendering an identifier |

The monospace rule, stated once so a builder does not have to infer it:

- Monospace: accessions (`NM_007294.4`), rsIDs (`rs334`), concept ids (`C0677776`), predicate names (`gene_associated_with_condition`), tool names (`ncbi_efetch`), dates, and record URLs.
- Proportional: gene symbols (BRCA1, GCK), disease names and abbreviations (MODY), evidence kinds ("curated assertion"), confidence values, and licence text ("public domain").

The test is not "is this biomedical" but "would someone copy or compare this character by character". A gene symbol inside a sentence is read as a word, and setting it in monospace makes the line stutter without telling the reader anything they need.

With these settled, the design review is complete and the phase can open on `phase/4.8-web-ui-visual-design`.
